articles.title: ¿Y si los Chiefs vuelven a ser los de siempre?
articles.standfirst: Versus ya los coloca entre los cinco favoritos a hacerse con la Super Bowl
articles.summary: Versus ya los coloca entre los cinco favoritos a hacerse con la Super Bowl
articles.body: Nueve meses después de que su temporada se hundiera con la rotura del ligamento cruzado de Patrick Mahomes, los Chiefs han vuelto a ser los Chiefs. Kansas City empieza 2026 con un 4-0 que la convierte, junto a los 49ers y los Vikings, en uno de los tres únicos equipos invictos de la NFL. Y el mercado de las casas de apuestas ya ha tomado nota. Versus los coloca entre los cinco principales candidatos al Vince Lombardi, a cuota 10. La caída fue tan dura como inesperada. En diciembre de 2025, Mahomes se lesionó la rodilla izquierda ante los Chargers, el equipo quedó eliminado de la pelea por los playoffs y se cortó una racha de diez años consecutivos clasificándose. La gran duda del verano era si el mariscal llegaría a tiempo y en qué estado. La respuesta está siendo la mejor posible. Mahomes volvió en el estreno de la temporada y el equipo no ha perdido desde entonces. Ganó en la prórroga a los Colts (33-30), con 382 yardas y tres touchdowns de su quarterback, se impuso por 24-10 en Miami y el domingo sumó un 30-27 en Las Vegas, en un duelo entre dos equipos invictos que decidió con dos touchdowns en apenas 19 segundos del último cuarto. Mahomes terminó con 225 yardas y dos pases de anotación, y Kenneth Walker III, la gran incorporación ofensiva, corrió para 177 yardas y otros dos touchdowns. Los Chiefs llegan así a su semana de descanso como líderes en solitario de la AFC Oeste y último equipo invicto de la conferencia. El dato añade valor histórico a la racha. Chiefs, 49ers y Vikings son los únicos equipos perfectos tras la Semana 4, y es la primera vez desde 2013 que dos equipos que no jugaron los playoffs el año anterior, Kansas City y Minnesota, empiezan la temporada con cuatro victorias. Por el camino han ido cayendo otros aspirantes: los Bills perdieron su invicto ante los Patriots y los Raiders, que llegaban con 3-0, dejaron escapar el partido en el último cuarto. El mercado de las apuestas deportivas ha reaccionado con reconocimiento, pero también con prudencia. Versus encabeza su lista con los Rams, a cuota 7, seguidos de los Bills, a 8, y de Ravens y 49ers, ambos a 9.5. Los Chiefs completan el quinteto a 10. Entre el primer favorito y el quinto hay una distancia mínima, lo que describe una temporada abierta de par en par. Lo más llamativo es precisamente quién lidera esa clasificación. Los Rams, máximos favoritos, arrancan con un 2-2 irregular. Los Bills, segundos en el mercado, están en 3-1 tras su caída en Nueva Inglaterra. Es decir, las dos primeras posiciones se sostienen más en el potencial de plantilla que en los resultados. Los 49ers, también a 9.5, llegan en la situación opuesta: 4-0, con la mejor diferencia de puntos de la NFC y el liderato de su división, lo que los convierte probablemente en el rival más directo de los Chiefs en términos de rendimiento real. Los argumentos a favor de Kansas City son sólidos. Cuenta con el mejor quarterback de su generación ya recuperado, con una ofensiva más equilibrada gracias a Walker y con una defensa que está sosteniendo los partidos apretados. Pero conviene no dejarse deslumbrar por el récord. Dos de sus cuatro triunfos han sido por solo tres puntos, y en varias ocasiones el equipo ha necesitado remontar o sufrir hasta el final. Mahomes todavía no ha recuperado las cifras más brillantes de otros años, y la lesión de Tyquan Thornton, protagonista en Las Vegas con 111 yardas y dos touchdowns, añade una preocupación a un vestuario que ya no puede permitirse más bajas.

articles.title: "I know how hard she works”: How Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle turned a business struggle into a five-venture empire while building her own path beyond the NHL spotlight
articles.summary: Lauren Kyle McDavid had always known she wanted to build something of her own, but turning her creative ideas into successful businesses came with a
articles.body: Lauren Kyle McDavid had always known she wanted to build something of her own, but turning her creative ideas into successful businesses came with a learning curve. The wife of Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid started with interior design before expanding into fashion, furniture, food and publishing. Behind that growth was a challenge she had to face early in her career: learning the business side of her creative work.That part of Lauren’s journey became more important as she took on more projects. By June 2025, she had several ventures under her name, while Connor had watched closely as she learned to turn her ideas into businesses. His support also came at a time when Lauren needed help taking her first company to the next level. Connor McDavid saw how hard Lauren Kyle was working behind the scenesLauren spoke about her entrepreneurial journey in a June 8, 2025 interview with theScore. She explained that she had always pictured herself working for herself and had grown up around people who ran their own businesses. Her first major venture was Kyle & Co., an interior design company that gave her a place to turn her ideas into a career.However, creativity alone could not handle every part of running a growing company. Connor explained during the same theScore interview that creative people can sometimes struggle with the business side of their ideas. He had seen Lauren put considerable time and energy into Kyle & Co. and wanted to help her move the company forward.“I know how hard she works, and I know the time and energy that she puts into it,” Connor said while discussing Lauren’s business journey with theScore in June 2025.Connor had also given Lauren sessions with a business coach as a birthday gift a few years earlier. The support proved useful because Lauren wanted to grow beyond her first company without losing the creative side that had driven her from the beginning.Lauren later explained just how valuable that experience became for her. “Without my business coach, I definitely wouldn't be able to have this many businesses at one time,” she told theScore in June 2025. She said the coaching helped change her mindset and gave her a better understanding of how to grow as an entrepreneur.Lauren Kyle used that lesson to expand far beyond interior designThe business coaching became part of a much bigger change in Lauren’s career. By June 2025, her portfolio included Kyle & Co., Sports Club Atelier, Trove Living and Bar Trove, while she was also preparing a cookbook.Sports Club Atelier grew from Lauren’s interest in creating better-looking sports apparel. Trove Living gave her interior design work a furniture and showroom component, while Bar Trove brought her creative approach into the restaurant space in downtown Edmonton. Her cookbook followed the same idea by focusing on experiences such as dinner parties and girls’ weekends instead of simply dividing recipes into traditional categories.Lauren’s approach has remained consistent across those projects. She wants people to feel something when they enter a space, wear something she designed or experience something she created. That idea also explains why Connor has remained impressed by the work happening behind the scenes.“I get a front row seat to everything she’s building,” Connor said in theScore’s June 2025 profile.Lauren’s story is therefore about more than being Connor McDavid’s wife. She had to learn a side of business that did not come naturally to her, accepted help when she needed it and used that experience to build a much larger portfolio of her own.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Juan Lebrón más líder: así fue la charla a su compañero que valió una victoria
articles.standfirst: El ‘Lobo’ tuvo unas bonitas palabras hacia Leo Augsburger en un momento de dudas y abajo en el marcador para terminar remontando el partido
articles.summary: El ‘Lobo’ tuvo unas bonitas palabras hacia Leo Augsburger en un momento de dudas y abajo en el marcador para terminar remontando el partido
articles.body: Desde sus inicios, Juan Lebrón ha sido un jugador polémico. Su pasión y competitividad le han hecho llegar a lo más alto, pero también le han jugado malas pasadas en ciertos momentos. No obstante, desde que está con Leo Augsburger se ve una versión más madura y calmada del gaditano, la cual ha vuelto a demostrar con una brutal reflexión en banquillos que sirvió para remontar un partido que tenían casi perdido. En la jornada de octavos de final, el ‘Lobo’ y su compañero se medían a Juanlu Esbrí e Iñigo Jofre. Dos jugadores de menor ranking, pero con mucho potencial para complicar a cualquiera. Era su estreno en el P2 de Düsseldorf, un torneo con una pista más lenta que otras del calendario. Un escenario que afecta especialmente a Augsburger, cuya mayor fortaleza radica en su capacidad para rematar. Venían además de caer en cuartos de final en Rotterdam ante Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas, por lo que no podían fallar. En el arranque, las sensaciones estaban siendo muy malas. Empezaron perdiendo el primer set con un Leo muy lejos de su nivel habitual. Se encendían las alarmas. Nada más empezar la segunda manga, break en contra y su pase a la siguiente ronda se ponía todavía más cuesta arriba. Una situación que en otros momentos habría sacado lo peor del ‘Lobo’, pero que en este caso hizo todo lo contrario. Con el marcador 2-1 abajo, Lebrón se sentó en el banquillo y, con máxima calma, alentó a su compañero. Su entrenador, Agustín Gómez Silingo empezó a dar instrucciones para acercarse al triunfo y el gaditano le paró: “Esto no va de táctica, va de que se relaje. Leo, necesito que estés tranquilo. Ve para adelante. Si tiro un globo paralelo, vas a bloquearlas todas. Es un tema mental. Disfruta, ‘gordo’”. Unas palabras que destensaron al posadeño. Desde ese momento, Augsburger jugó mucho más suelto y, aunque no tuvo su día más brillante, comenzó a ganar más puntos. Siguió cometiendo algunos errores, pero ya con la confianza de tener el apoyo de su compañero incluso en los momentos más complicados. Nada más salir del banquillo, igualaron el break que tenían en contra y se llevaron el segundo set por 6-3. “No me importa ganar o perder, pero tenemos que ser un equipo”, expresó el ‘Lobo’ más tarde. Minutos después de la charla, Gómez Silingo le reconoció a Juan el mérito: “Necesitaba lo que vos hiciste. Fue lo que destrabó la situación. Necesito que sigas liderando así”. Y es que, unas simples palabras le quitaron a Leo un gran peso de encima y finalmente fueron capaces de llevarse el triunfo por 3-6, 6-3 y 6-3, clasificándose a los cuartos de final en tierras alemanas.

articles.title: Vikings Star Justin Jefferson Gushes Over Chance To Play With Odell Beckham Jr.
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings superstar Justin Jefferson was all smiles talking about the team adding veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr.
articles.body: Justin Jefferson and Odell Beckham Jr. have a few things in common. First, they each played their collegiate ball with the LSU Tigers. Second, they've each been superstar wide receivers in the NFL. And now, they're teammates on the Minnesota Vikings, and the 27-year-old Jefferson is thrilled to be teammates with the veteran Beckham. "It's definitely cool," Jefferson said in a press conference on Wednesday afternoon about the Vikings signing Beckham. "All of the years I've watched him play and looked up to his game and his play style, both on and off the field, how he carries himself as a superstar in the league and just managing it. We've been brothers for a very, very long time. The connection has always been there. We've always kind of talked about this moment and one day being able to play with each other, but for it to actually be here is definitely crazy. "He called me last night to tell me that he was coming down and just the excitement on his face and just the excitement that we both share together, it was definitely a cool moment." Minnesota signed Beckham to its practice squad Wednesday, which comes in the wake of Jefferson missing the team's Week 4 win over the Miami Dolphins with an ankle injury. Beckham, who was a Pro Bowler with the New York Giants from 2014-16 and spent the first five seasons of his NFL career with the Giants (2014-18), was released by New York last week after logging just one target in the team's first three games. Beckham didn't play in 2025. Prior to the aforementioned gap year, he had one-year stints with the Miami Dolphins (2024) and Baltimore Ravens (2023), preceded by missing the 2022 season due to a torn ACL and helping the Los Angeles Rams win the Super Bowl in 2021; the Giants traded Beckham to the Browns in 2019, with the receiver playing two-plus years in Cleveland before being waived during the 2021 season and joining the Rams. Over the three games he has played this season, Jefferson, a two-time All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowler, has totaled 13 receptions for 179 yards and two touchdowns. While Minnesota is 4-0, its offense has struggled, as the Vikings are last in the NFL in passing yards (156.0 per game), 31st in total yards (262.8 per game), 18th in points (21.5 per game) and 16th in rushing yards (106.8 per game). Beckham, who played in Baton Rouge from 2011-13, is ninth in LSU history with 2,340 receiving yards and was selected by the Giants with the No. 12 pick in the 2014 NFL Draft after a standout junior season that saw him average 19.5 yards per reception. Jefferson, Beckham and the Vikings have a road matchup against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 (Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX).

articles.title: Carey Price signed an $84 million NHL contract: How the Montreal Canadiens legend built his fortune through a remarkable career, record-breaking seasons and historic legacy
articles.summary: Explore Carey Price's remarkable NHL career and his $84 million contract, detailing how his achievements on the ice contributed to his wealth and enduring legacy with the Montreal Canadiens.
articles.body: As Price’s wealth grew, so did his reputation as one of the NHL’s top goalies. Drafted fifth overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 2005 NHL Draft, Price immediately became the team’s long-term building block and one of the highest paid players in the sport. His biggest financial milestone arrived in July 2017, when Montreal committed $84 million to him over eight years.The contract gave Price an average annual value of $10.5 million and featured a heavily front-loaded salary structure with substantial signing bonuses. Those terms became particularly important during the final years of his career, when recurring knee problems prevented him from returning to NHL action. According to Celebrity Net Worth, Price has an estimated net worth of $40 million, although career salary databases put his NHL earnings substantially higher.Carey Price built an NHL fortune through one historic contractThe foundation of Price's fortune was the eight-year, $84 million extension signed with the Montreal Canadiens on July 2, 2017. The agreement began with the 2018-19 season and carried a $10.5 million annual average value, placing Price among the NHL's highest-paid players and making him the league's highest-paid goaltender at the time.The contract was structured differently from a simple $10.5 million annual salary. A large portion of the money was delivered through signing bonuses, including $13 million in each of the first two seasons. The deal then included additional bonuses of $8.75 million, $11 million, $6.75 million, $6.5 million and $5.5 million in subsequent seasons.Contract detailCarey PriceTeamMontreal CanadiensContract length8 yearsTotal value84millionAverageannualvalue10.5 millionSigning dateJuly 2, 2017Contract period2018-19 to 2025-26That structure meant Price's actual yearly compensation varied considerably despite the consistent $10.5 million cap hit. His first two seasons under the agreement each carried $15 million in total salary, including the $13 million signing bonus. The 2021-22 season also reached $13 million in total compensation.Carey Price's career earnings extended beyond $120 millionPrice's $84 million extension represented only one major chapter of his NHL earnings. Before signing it, the Canadiens had already committed $39 million to him through a six-year contract signed in 2012. His earlier deals, entry-level compensation and subsequent payments pushed his career salary total far beyond the headline value of his 2017 extension.Different salary databases produce slightly different totals depending on methodology and whether figures are adjusted or categorized differently. HockeyZonePlus lists Price's career NHL earnings at approximately $128.77 million, while PuckPedia estimates career earnings at around $131.01 million. Celebrity Net Worth, meanwhile, lists his current net worth at $40 million.The difference between career earnings and net worth is important, and career earnings represent money generated through playing contracts, while net worth reflects assets, investments, taxes, spending and other financial considerations. As a result, the two figures should not be treated as interchangeable.Carey Price career success strengthened his NHL legacyPrice's financial value was closely connected to what he accomplished on the ice. The 2014-15 season represented the high point of his individual career and helped establish the reputation that ultimately supported his landmark contract.That season, Price won the Hart Memorial Trophy, awarded to the NHL's most valuable player, and the Vezina Trophy, given to the league's top goaltender, and he also received the Ted Lindsay Award and William M. Jennings Trophy, completing an extraordinary collection of individual honors.The Canadiens goaltender posted a 1.96 goals-against average and .933 save percentage that season. It figures that placed him firmly among the NHL's elite. His performances also helped Montreal remain competitive during an era when Price had become the team's most important defensive presence.Carey Price became a defining Montreal Canadiens figurePrice's relationship with Montreal also played a major role in his earning power, rather than moving between several NHL franchises, he spent his entire NHL career with the Canadiens, becoming one of the most recognizable faces of the organisation.His franchise statistics underline that influence. Price finished his Montreal career with 361 wins and 712 games played, both all-time Canadiens records for a goaltender. He also recorded 49 shutouts for the franchise.His six NHL All-Star selections and First-Team All-Star recognition in 2014-15 further demonstrate how consistently he was regarded among the league's best goaltenders, and his performance also helped Montreal reach the 2021 Stanley Cup Final, giving Price one of the most memorable playoff runs of his career.Carey Price earnings continued through long-term injury tenureThe final stage of Price's career was defined less by games played and more by the security of the contract he had negotiated years earlier. After his April 2022 appearance, continuing knee problems prevented him from returning to NHL competition. Montreal nevertheless remained responsible for the guaranteed financial commitments within his contract.The annual structure illustrates how substantial those commitments remained. Price's contract called for $7.75 million in 2022-23, $8.5 million in 2023-24 and $7.5 million in each of the final two seasons. Much of those amounts came through signing bonuses rather than traditional base salary.The contract's final years also became part of a salary-cap management decision for Montreal. In September 2025, the Canadiens traded Price and a 2026 fifth-round draft pick to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for defenseman prospect Gannon Laroque. Price had not played since 2022 and was entering the final season of his eight-year agreement.Price’s financial legacy is more than his headline-grabbing contract, with his NHL earnings a product of a series of deals over nearly two decades and endorsement opportunities providing another stream of income. Celebrity Net Worth identifies brand partnerships as part of his broader financial profile, alongside his playing contracts.More importantly, Price's career demonstrates how elite performance can translate into long-term financial security. The $84 million extension was awarded when Montreal believed its franchise goaltender remained one of the most valuable players at his position. His subsequent injuries changed the final chapter of his playing career, but they did not diminish the financial significance of the deal.For Montreal, Price remains the franchise's all-time leader in wins and games played by a goaltender. For the NHL, his career represents the combination of elite performance, long-term contract security and unprecedented compensation for a goaltender during his prime.And for Carey Price, the $84 million deal that was a reward for years of elite goaltending is the financial legacy most tied to his name. On the ice, his Hart and Vezina-winning 2014-15 campaign and Montreal records established his status as a franchise icon. Together, those achievements explain why his career remains one of the defining financial and sporting stories of the modern Canadiens era.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Roman Reigns sends a heartfelt personal message of support and encouragement to WWE fans targeted by bullying
articles.summary: WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns has reached out to young fans who recently became victims of bullying.
articles.body: WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns has reached out to young fans who recently became victims of bullying. The WWE star has extended his heartfelt personal message of support and encouragement to WWE fans targeted by bullying. A fan was bullied and assaulted while playing basketball at the North Charleston Community Center. After learning about the situation, Reigns recorded a personal video message for KShawn. The WWE star assured him that he had the support of the WWE community and encouraged him to remain strong. Let's take a look at the situation more closely that what prompted Reigns to extend his support.Roman Reigns extends support to an autistic fan who was a victim of bullying and assaultWWE Superstar Roman Reigns has extended his support to a young autistic fan who was recently targeted in a bullying and assault incident. The fan, KShawn Foye, a semi-verbal autistic man, was reportedly attacked while playing basketball at the North Charleston Community Center.The victim's attackers broke his headphones and struck him in a video which was posted by his mother, Kimberly, to bring awareness to the matter. After learning about the situation, Reigns personally reached out to KShawn with a heartfelt message.The former Undisputed WWE Universal Champion assured the fan that he had the support of the WWE community and encouraged him to remain strong despite the difficult experience.In the video, Reigns stated, “Good friend, a little birdy told me that you’ve been having a little trouble and there’s some stuff at school, and some of the kids are bullying you. I just want you to know that all your friends here at WWE are with you. I know it can be tough. Life can be unfair sometimes, it really can, but I just want you to know that we are thinking about you.”He further added, Keep your head up, just know that you are the man. You are a good kid. And we know you mean the best, and we just want to reward you for all the support you send our way, and we want you to understand that we are supporting you as well.Roman Reigns also invited the young fan to one of his wrestling events. He confirmed by saying, “So, I’m going to do my very best to make it happen. And whenever WWE is coming near you, you’re going to be at the show. And trust me, you’re gonna have some Tribal Chief tickets. They’re gonna be the best seats in the house. So, make sure you enjoy yourself. And I’m going to keep tabs on you to make sure everything’s all good, man”Meanwhile, Roman Reigns is officially set to be part of WWE Survivor Series 2026, with the company continuing to build its plans around the World Heavyweight Champion. articles.title: BFI headed for showdown: Secretary general calls SGM to move no-confidence motion against federation chief
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Boxing Federation of India (BFI) is headed for a showdown, with secretary general Pramod Kumar convening a Special General Meeting (SGM) on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Boxing Federation of India (BFI) is headed for a showdown, with secretary general Pramod Kumar convening a Special General Meeting (SGM) on Oct 24 to move a no-confidence motion against president Ajay Singh, even as Singh said the federation’s priority must remain the preparation of its boxers for the Los Angeles Olympics.The notice, issued to affiliated state units, lists alleged unilateral decision-making, unauthorised constitutional amendments, intimidation of state associations, financial irregularities, administrative overreach and conflicts with elected office-bearers among the grounds for the motion. TOI has a copy of the motion. It has been learnt that 28 of BFI’s 35 state member units are signatories to the no-confidence motion.Kumar has also issued a cease-and-desist notice to BFI executive director Col Arun Malik, asking him to stop acting at Singh’s behest or authority, particularly in matters falling within the secretary general’s constitutional domain. Malik has also been asked to stop accessing or using the secretary general’s official email account without authorisation. Kumar warned of legal action if the alleged conduct continues.Singh, however, responded strongly and sought to shift the focus to the athletes. “Our focus must remain on our boxers and their preparation for the Olympics. BFI will do everything within its power to give them the support and conditions they need to succeed. We will take the strongest possible action against any attempt to disrupt their preparation or hinder the progress of Indian boxing,” he said.A key point of contention is the constitutional provision governing an SGM. The BFI constitution currently available on its website states that an SGM may be called by the president or upon a request from two-thirds of the Executive Committee, with the meeting to be convened within 30 days of such a request.The rival camp, however, has cited another BFI constitution, which it says is government-approved. It states that an SGM shall be convened by the secretary general on receiving a written requisition from the president or at least 15 members, or on the direction of the Executive Council, with the meeting to be held 20-30 days after receipt of the requisition.The Singh camp has maintained that the latter is an old constitution that no longer exists or has any bearing, and that the version currently on the BFI website is the operative constitution approved by World Boxing.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Erling Haaland Wants Manchester City Fans To Be United Amid Guilty Verdict
articles.summary: Erling Haaland has called on everyone at Manchester City to “stick together" in his first public comments since the club was found guilty of large-scale financial rule-breaking.
articles.body: Erling Haaland called on everyone at Manchester City to "stick together" in his first public comments since the club was found guilty of large-scale financial rule-breaking in the Premier League. City will play Liverpool on Sunday in its first match since the publication of an investigatory panel’s verdict that City artificially inflated its revenue by more than $1 billion from 2009-18 to circumvent financial fair-play rules that restricted rival clubs in that period. City was found guilty by the panel of all 80 of the serious financial charges brought by the Premier League and could be hit with severe sanctions — including being expelled from the top flight. City has lodged an appeal against the findings. In an interview with Sky Sports published Thursday, Haaland — City's most high-profile player — said: "We have to stick together and we have to spread the love to each other. So yeah, stick together, enjoy the ride and smile." Asked what his message would be to City fans traveling to Anfield, where a potentially hostile reception awaits the team, Haaland said: "We have to stick together, we have to stay with each other and we have to stay positive. "No matter what happens in life, we have always have to have a smile. So we have to stay positive, look ahead and try to win football games and then try to enjoy the situation and the game." City manager Enzo Maresca is likely to face more severe questioning Friday when he holds his pre-match news conference with reporters. It will be Maresca's first remarks on the scandal, with domestic soccer having been on hold for the past three weeks because of an extended international break. Premier League Managers Speak On Man City Case The return of the Premier League offers rival team coaches a first opportunity to react to the City case that has rocked the world’s most popular soccer league and is likely to have a major impact on the remainder of the season. They weren't rushing to judgment on Thursday. "We’ve all seen the news. It’s obviously big news," said Frank Lampard, the Coventry manager who played for City for one of the seasons — 2014-15 — that has been under investigation. "Man City are appealing the situation so I guess my reaction is that: what can you say when an appeal is going on? I’m not inside the story, I’m outside it completely — I played for Man City a long time ago, for one year — so we’ll wait and see what the result of the appeal is." Bournemouth manager Marco Rose preferred to stay away from the matter, saying: "I’m a football coach, not a politician," while Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle said he was "not able to judge" as a manager of another club and "there are authorities taking care of it." In a similar vein, Leeds manager Daniel Farke said there were "more qualified people ... able to speak about it." Speaking at the Leaders in Sport conference in London, Leeds chairman Paraag Marathe – president of the club’s U.S.-ownership group, 49ers Enterprises – said he believed "the most just result, I’m sure, will be delivered." "In any sport, you know, everybody wants to play by the same rules," he added, without mentioning City. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Sean Payton Says He’ll Call Broncos’ Offensive Plays Against Chargers
articles.summary: Broncos' coach Sean Payton told reporters that he will be calling the plays starting this Sunday against the Chargers
articles.body: Even with a talented quarterback in Bo Nix and a new wide receiver in Jaylen Waddle, the Denver Broncos’ offense still hasn't delivered. Payton told reporters that he will be calling the plays starting this Sunday against the Chargers. ESPN had originally reported that offensive coordinator Davis Webb will still be the main communication with Nix, but Payton would have the final say. Denver fell to the Chiefs in its Week 1 road opener, 31-10, in Patrick Mahomes' return from injury; it then secured home wins over the Jaguars in Week 2 and the Rams in Week 3, but suffered its second loss to the 49ers on the road. That puts the Broncos at 2-2, with both losses resulting from 14 points or fewer on offense, calling for a new solution in play-calling. Webb got the keys to play-calling this offseason, with Payton still close by. But Payton made it clear that offensive play-calling needed a change moving forward. "I think our focus needs to be more on the specifics and the detail of each play regardless [of who's calling the plays]. I think Davis is very fast, very quick, and understands what we're doing. I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the whys," according to ESPN. Payton's involvement will help Denver’s offense improve across the board, given its numbers after Week 4. The Broncos’ run game ranks 29th in yards per game with 81, and the offense ranks 27th in yards per game with 280. Noticing glaring issues early on, Payton noted that correcting them quickly will be vital down the road. "I think, collectively, we all after a game, and after a four-game sample size, certainly this isn't championship football, what we see. How quickly can we correct those things?" With a Week 6 showdown with the Seattle Seahawks, who sit atop the league in yards allowed per game with 246, implementing Payton in a larger play-calling role in Week 5 will be the prime setup heading into a home game vs. Seattle’s defense.

articles.title: Arsenal starlet Lisa Baum (19) looks forward to first Germany senior team cap
articles.summary: There has not been much time for Lisa Baum to stop and take stock. A year ago, the teenage winger was still establishing herself at RB Leipzig. This summer,...
articles.body:
There has not been much time for Lisa Baum to stop and take stock. A year ago, the teenage winger was still establishing herself at RB Leipzig. This summer, Arsenal paid a reported Bundesliga-record €600,000 to take her to North London. Five league starts, two goals and one senior Germany call-up later, the 19-year-old suddenly finds herself preparing for another potential milestone.

"Yes, there's a lot going on as of late," Baum remarked at Germany's pre-match press conference this week.

That may qualify as something of an understatement.

Baum has risen from German youth football to one of Europe's biggest clubs and the senior national team at remarkable speed. Yet, when asked to reflect on the journey, she speaks less about the size of the stages now confronting her than the places she came from.

"I'm very grateful for the place that I began at [Hamburg] and the place where I developed further [Leipzig]," Baum said. "I think the key was to be patient and be myself. I think about home a lot as my family still lives there."

Those two ideas – patience and remaining herself – run neatly through Baum's story.

From Tanzania and Ahrensbök to the Bundesliga

Baum was born in Tanzania in 2006 to a Tanzanian mother and German father. She moved to the small Schleswig-Holstein town of Ahrensbök at the age of five and began playing football with boys at local club MTV Ahrensbök.

Baum moved on to Pansdorf, then Hamburg, before eventually arriving at RB Leipzig in 2025. The more important part of her Leipzig year concerned everything else. Head coach Jonas Stephan later admitted that there had initially been a small question over how Baum would respond to the demands required to turn obvious talent into an elite career.

"After one week of training, I knew who we had signed," Stephan remarked in an interview with Kicker . "She understood how hard she has to work."

Leipzig worked heavily on Baum's defensive game and physical output. She occasionally featured at wing-back, learned to expend more energy without the ball and gradually improved the running numbers that initially required work.

Baum embraced it. The results became increasingly evident after the winter break. Eight of Baum's nine scorer points during the 2025/26 campaign arrived after the turn of the year as she developed from promising talent into one of Leipzig's decisive attacking players.

By the summer, keeping her was no longer realistic.

Record move to Arsenal quickly justified

Arsenal won a race involving several major European clubs and paid €600,000 to bring Baum to England. Even that step has so far looked surprisingly comfortable. Baum started each of Arsenal's opening five league fixtures. She scored the winner away at Brighton on the opening day and later added another goal against Manchester City.

Established internationals have found themselves competing with the teenager for minutes. Arsenal striker Alessia Russo offered an early indication of how highly Baum was already regarded. Asked at the PFA Awards which teammate might find herself attending the ceremony the following year, Russo named the club's new German winger.

The football itself remains recognizable. Baum still wants the ball at her feet. She still attacks defenders directly. She can operate naturally from the left or start on the right before driving inside onto her stronger foot. Her low passes into attacking areas and willingness to shoot give her game a directness that Germany head coach Christian Wück has also noticed.

Baum herself traces much of that style back to something considerably less structured than an Arsenal training session.

"My way of playing football came a lot from playing on the local pitch," she explained this week. "Just playing freely when you aren't really thinking about anything."

Germany call-up fulfils a childhood dream

Wück rewarded Baum's Arsenal start with her first senior Germany call-up for the October friendlies against Australia and Japan. She had previously collected five U23 caps. The senior invitation represented, in Baum's words, a "childhood dream."

Her arrival also offers Germany something slightly different. Wück now has a naturally left-footed wide attacker capable of operating on either flank and attacking inward from the right. A senior debut could follow against Australia in Karlsruhe.

Rapid movement has not translated into detachment. Baum remains connected with the clubs and people involved earlier in her career.

"I still visit my old clubs and the old friends that I have there," she said. "I still follow HSV [women]. I just watched them against Wolfsburg [last weekend]. I like watching HSV."

That attachment mirrors what people from Ahrensbök say about her. Her former youth coach Kai Schmütz told Kicker that Baum still keeps in touch and returns when her schedule permits. For a player whose career has accelerated so dramatically, he views that as evidence that very little has changed underneath it.

There have also been considerably harder experiences along the way. Baum lost her 17-year-old brother in a car accident in 2022. She has previously spoken about wearing his name on tape during matches and carrying his initials on her boots.

The loss remains part of her story without defining the footballer she has become. Those who worked with Baum in Leipzig instead repeatedly return to her openness, humour, courage and willingness to work. Stephan went considerably further.

"If she keeps that up," the Leipzig coach said of Baum's mentality in his Kicker interview. "She will certainly become one of the greatest players in the world."

That is an enormous projection for any 19-year-old.

articles.title: Harrison Moore takes ownership after Florida's run game stalls
articles.summary: Harrison Moore assessed Florida's offensive-line struggles at Missouri, Jadan Baugh's difficult game and the response needed against South Carolina.
articles.body:
Harrison Moore did not let Jadan Baugh shoulder the blame after Florida 's running game disappeared at Missouri.

The veteran offensive lineman said Florida failed to give Baugh a fair opportunity to produce during the 45-17 loss, accepting responsibility for a performance in which the Gators were out-physicaled at the line of scrimmage.

Moore also discussed the team's angry but focused return to practice, the discipline required to reduce penalties and the opportunity to respond against South Carolina during homecoming weekend.

Where Florida's Aaron Philo ranks among first-year starting quarterbacks

How frustrating was Florida's performance against Missouri?

It's always tough when you go out there and don't perform the way you want to. Obviously, we definitely didn't execute the way we wanted.

But the biggest thing is that it's a new week and a new opportunity. That wasn't our last game of the season. We still have a lot of the season left. We get another opportunity Saturday, and our objective is to go out there and play the best ball we can.

What was different about the offensive line's performance?

Like I said, it was execution. We didn't execute our jobs to the best of our ability. I think, at points, they out-physicaled us and out-strained us. It boils down to the preparation at the start of the week. We've got to do better with that.

How consistent is Sumrall's message following wins and losses?

He's the same every single day. That's something he said to us today: "I would come in and tell you the same thing whether we won or lost. It's a new week, and we're starting fresh."

Whether we won by 40 or lost by 40, it's a new week. Learn from the mistakes, which, unfortunately, there were a lot of. It's a new week, and we'll do everything we can to execute Saturday.

How did Baugh respond to his performance?

He came up and talked to us and said, "Look, I'm sorry. I need to do better." The first thing I said to him was, "No, I need to do better. We didn't give you the opportunity to play to the best of your ability."

As the running back, he's the one who is going to receive a lot of the criticism from the media. But ultimately, as an offensive line, we didn't give him the opportunity to be who he is.

He was getting hit at the line of scrimmage a lot, with two or three tacklers on the ball. That boils down to us not doing our job.

I talked to him today, and he was pretty positive. Like I said, it's about moving on to the next week. We're going to get everything right, and tomorrow we're going to have a great practice. That's where it really starts.

I would say it was very focused. There was a lot of stuff we needed to clean up. Everybody was a little pissed off. They woke up angry this morning, especially me. There's a lot of stuff I need to do better.

The best opportunity I have to improve is right now during practice. I think we did a good job of having an intentional Monday. That's going to carry over to Tuesday's practice, getting better with every snap.

How can Florida reduce the penalties that have increased during SEC play?

Discipline. I think it starts off the field. Make sure we're showing up to meetings on time. Make sure we're dressed correctly in meetings. Make sure we're living right off the field.

A lot of the stuff that comes up on Saturdays — the little penalties and little stupid stuff — starts during the week. We need to do a better job of making sure everybody is 100% clean during the week and doing the right things.

Can Florida grow more from a loss than a win?

Absolutely. Sometimes when you win, it's tough to look at those mistakes and really harp on them because you think, "We won." Sometimes I have a bad block, but Jadan takes it 60 yards to the house. A good thing happened, so I'm not really going to focus on the bad thing.

But when you lose, especially the way we did, you look at everything and really fine-tune it. I watched the film four or five times. I kept rewatching plays and rewatching plays. It's definitely easier to get after it following a loss.

I think I could have done a better job after the big win against Ole Miss of still focusing on those mistakes. Ultimately, it's a new week. I'm excited to go out there and play Saturday.

How can the team improve its maturity during the season?

Like I said, it starts during the week. It starts Monday by making sure everybody is here. We all showed up and had a great lift. Then it goes into Tuesday. It's really one day at a time and one rep at a time. Focus on where your feet are and do as much as you can to become as good as you can during that moment.

How did Aaron Philo respond to the loss?

I think he did a really good job of wiping the slate clean. He talked to us after our lift, brought the whole team together and said, "Don't let this loss separate us."

That's the biggest thing. If we let this break us apart, who knows where we'll be four games from now? We need to let this loss bring us closer together, really bond as a team, learn from our mistakes and execute Saturday.

It was very similar to what I've been saying: It's a new slate, and we get another opportunity this weekend. The biggest thing was execution. A lot of the stuff we didn't do well was self-inflicted. That can't happen, especially at this level. We aren't going to be able to win games if we don't execute. That's what it really boils down to every single day.

How confident are you that Florida's defense will make the necessary corrections?

One hundred percent. I have complete faith in the guys on that side of the ball and the coaches. They play their butts off every single day in practice.

It wasn't just them. Nobody had a good game. Obviously, a lot of people are going to point fingers and all that. Everybody needs to take a mental reset and prepare as well as we can this week so we can execute Saturday.

How does the offense maintain confidence when players such as Brown and Stockton are unavailable?

It boils down to preparation and making sure whoever is stepping up is ready to play. That's something we talk about a lot: Next man up.

You're one play away from being the starter, being the guy or having your role change. Make sure you have complete confidence in the playbook and complete confidence in the offense. That's something we worked on all offseason — making sure everybody is ready to play multiple positions.

What does returning to The Swamp for homecoming mean to you?

I love the muddy games. It means we get to run the football, which I love. It's going to be a physical football game. South Carolina is a really good team up front, so it will be a good challenge for us.

I love playing in The Swamp. This place is something really, really special. I haven't been here for a long time, but you can tell every time you step into that place. Even when I came here on my official visit during the spring, with nobody in there, you could feel the history.

When you walk past that gator by the locker room, you feel all the history, the people and the national championships that have come through that building. I'm really excited to get another opportunity in The Swamp.

articles.title: Yankees fans should buckle up for the latest on Aaron Boone's future
articles.summary: Following a disappointing exit in the ALDS against the Rays, the New York Yankees' plans for manager Aaron Boone may not be what fans want to hear.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees fell short of the World Series for the 16th time in the last 17 seasons, also marking their 17th consecutive year without a World Series victory. The 2026 loss came at the hands of the Tampa Bay Rays in a 3-0 sweep, raising questions about what lies ahead for the Yankees, especially as fans wonder about the future of manager Aaron Boone and potentially general manager Brian Cashman.

For the many frustrated Yankees fans who have called for a change at manager, specifically, the latest comments from Buster Olney on ESPN New York's Dipietro & Rothenberg may not be what you want to hear. Olney addressed the potential for any significant changes and admitted he doesn't expect any change regarding Boone or Cashman.

"Look, I know that there's always a lot of conversation when the Yankees lose around the manager," Olney said. "There are certainly organizations where it feels like that there are fissures and fractures between the owner and the general manager and the manager. I have not seen one [with the Yankees]. You talk to Brian Cashman and Aaron Boone is his guy, and we know through actions, through the 30-year relationship, that Brian Cashman is Hal Steinbrenner's guy. So my guess is there won't be a change."

articles.body:
Can Michigan State football pick up its first win in nearly a month on Saturday afternoon? The Spartans Wire crew is mixed on the chances of that happening.

Michigan State is reeling at the moment in desperate need of a victory against Illinois this upcoming weekend. The Spartans have lost three straight games and come into this game with an overall record of 2-3 overall and 0-2 in Big Ten play.

Illinois is also stumbling into this game, with back-to-back conference losses to open Big Ten play. Illinois is 2-3 overall like the Spartans.

Kickoff for this matchup between Michigan State and Illinois is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET from Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. This game will be televised on FS1.

Let's take a look at our predictions for this week's matchup between Michigan State and Illinois below:

Prediction: Michigan State 9, Illinois 7

It's the movable force meets the resistable object. It's unfortunately time to accept that Michigan State is fully in a rebuilding year. However, Illinois is also pretty terrible. It's going to be a rock fight, but I'm giving MSU the edge at home.

Prediction: Illinois 27, Michigan State 20

Neither of these teams are very good at the moment, hence, why the betting line has this game as essentially a pick'em at this point in the week. I trust the Illinois offense a little bit more than the Spartans' right now, though, and that'll be the difference in this game. I'll say it again this week, I need to see it before I can believe in it with this Spartans' offense. Last week only further proved that theory...

Prediction: Michigan State 25, Illinois 22

I'm calling my shot here. These are two teams that are reeling, desperate for a win, and I think Fitzgerald and MSU's desperation is going to trump the Fighting Illini's. These are a couple of bad football teams, but it is now or never for both to show that they can salvage this season.

articles.title: Can Sean Miller Turn Texas Into an SEC Title Contender?
articles.summary: After suffering a heartbreaking loss to Purdue in the Sweet 16, Sean Miller's challenge at Texas this year will be turning a talented roster into one ready t...
articles.body:
After suffering a heartbreaking loss to Purdue in the Sweet 16, Sean Miller's challenge at Texas this year will be turning a talented roster into one ready to contend for an SEC championship. The Longhorns' frontcourt size and scoring options give Texas fans reason to be excited.

Texas' success will ultimately depend on how these talented players gel. Reliable guard play, relentless defense, and being able to close out tight games will be crucial if this team wants to finish at the top of the SEC. For this team to achieve its goal of taking home an SEC title, Miller will need to form lineups that can play together when shots are not falling.

Sean Miller enters his second year at Texas with a loaded roster. The Longhorns have an elite frontcourt featuring key returner Matas Vokietaitis , who had an outstanding finish to last year's season. Vokietaitis serves as the team's defensive anchor and has elite rim-protecting and rebounding abilities.

Last season, the big man from Lithuania averaged 15.6 ppg and 7.1 rebounds per game on 61.9% from the field. Vokietaitis boosted his averages during tournament play. He averaged 16 PPG and 8 rebounds. His return to this Texas squad gives them an elite rebounder. The big man also does an excellent job of using his seven-foot frame to clean the boards and create and convert on second efforts.

One of the best pickups in the portal was Texas landing TCU transfer David Punch. Last season, Punch was arguably the most impactful player on a solid TCU team.

Punch is known to be a bruiser inside who loves to use his strength and physicality. Standing at 6'7 and weighing 245 lbs, he rises to the occasion when guarding bigger defenders in the low post. This will allow Vokietaitis to be more of a weakside presence and help defenders who can roam the paint more freely.

Punch uses his physicality to set strong screens on defenders, creating easy scoring chances for himself and easy offense for his team. The junior forward is a nightmare on defense as he is always wearing down his opponents.

The Longhorns know they are getting an impact player in Punch. Last season, he averaged 14.1 ppg and 6.8 rebounds per game. This adds another inside presence for the Longhorns.

One of the most surprising events was Texas landing one of the top prospects in the class of 2027, Marcus Spears Jr. Not many people in the sport expected him to reclass and be part of this freshman class.

Spears is an elite athlete who gives Texas improved spacing on offense and a versatile defender who can switch onto and guard multiple positions. Miller will look to use Spears in small-ball lineups on occasion, which allows for the Longhorns to play at a faster pace.

Spears runs the floor well and can attack the basket off the bounce, giving Texas another scorer and another avenue to create offense. His passing ability and touch inside will help as he continues to develop his outside shot.

Texas will also have elite guard play this year. Miller landed McDonald's All-American Austin Goosby. The incoming freshman has an elite first step that allows him to get by defenses when they collapse or try to run him off the line.

With Mikey Lewis sidelined for some time, Goosby will likely take on a heavier load at the beginning of the season. Miller will be counting on his freshman guard to create shots, initiate the offense, and use his length to spread defenses out.

Goosby's elite shooting ability may discourage defenses from crowding Vokietaitis and Punch inside the paint. His ability to move without the ball and make cuts gives Texas another way of scoring without Goosby needing the ball.

Miller's roster has both elite spacing and players who know their roles. These small aspects of team building can haunt other teams. By doing this, Miller is ahead of the other top teams. Goosby will need to serve as the engine of this offense. With his six-foot-five frame, elite court vision, and ability to drive past his defender and get downhill, Goosby will be able to find Vokietaitis for easy points off dump-off passes or use drives and kicks to find open shooters.

Both Punch and Spears are elite at crashing the glass. They do a great job of converting second-chance opportunities. Having an elite inside presence on defense like Vokietaitis and an athletic wing like Spears allows the perimeter defenders to play more aggressively and speed up opposing offenses, which leads to turnovers and easy transition points. This Texas roster can wear opposing offenses down come SEC play.

There is no question that Texas has the talent to win an SEC championship. However, their success will come down to what lineups Miller decides to roll out. The Texas frontcourt gives them a solid foundation, while their reliable guard play can prevent their opponents from dominating the paint. Depending on freshmen means that Miller and his staff will be fine with freshman mistakes.

If Texas can produce lineups that take care of the ball, defend, and stretch defenses out, they will be a dangerous team in the SEC. The ability to be consistent will take them far this season and help them take down the reigning SEC champs , Florida.

articles.title: Inspiring story on family: “My road to success began the day my grandfather and his wife officially adopted my sister and me”-  Simone Biles reflects on the people who shaped her journey
articles.summary: For Simone Biles, success did not begin with an Olympic gold medal, a world championship title or a difficult gymnastics routine.
articles.body: For Simone Biles, success did not begin with an Olympic gold medal, a world championship title or a difficult gymnastics routine. Long before she became one of the most famous gymnasts in the world, her life took a major turn when her grandparents stepped in and gave her and her younger sister, Adria, a stable home. Biles has often spoken about how important that moment was in her life, especially because she and her siblings had spent time in foster care after their biological mother struggled to care for them. Her maternal grandfather, Ron Biles, and his wife, Nellie, eventually adopted Simone and Adria and raised them in Spring, Texas. Her quote, “My road to success began the day my grandfather and his wife officially adopted my sister and me,” says much more than it appears to at first. It is not simply about the legal moment when she became their daughter. For Biles, it represents the beginning of a safer childhood, a stronger support system and the chance to discover what she could become. Her story also shows that sometimes the people who change our lives are the ones who simply decide to stay, support us and give us the confidence to move forward.What happened before Simone Biles was adopted by her grandparents?Simone Biles was born in Columbus, Ohio, in 1997. Her early childhood was not easy. Her biological mother, Shanon Biles, struggled with drug and alcohol dependency, and Simone and her siblings spent time in foster care. During that period, her grandparents became an important source of comfort and stability. Biles has remembered being especially excited whenever her grandfather visited her while she was in foster care.Ron Biles and Nellie Biles eventually took Simone and her younger sister, Adria, into their home. Ron was Simone’s maternal grandfather, while Nellie was his wife. The couple later legally adopted both girls, while another relative took care of Simone’s older siblings.This was a major change for a young Simone. She was no longer moving through an uncertain situation and wondering where she would live. She had a home where she could grow up with people who were committed to her. The adoption also gave her something that would become extremely important as she grew older: a dependable support system.The story becomes even more meaningful when looking at how Biles viewed the relationship. She did not grow up thinking of Ron and Nellie as people who had simply rescued her. They became her parents in every way that mattered to her. Biles has previously explained that she considered being adopted normal because it was the life she knew. She did not spend her childhood feeling that something was missing.Why does Simone Biles describe her adoption as the beginning of her success?When Biles talks about her adoption as the beginning of her road to success, she is pointing to everything that happened after that turning point. Success did not arrive overnight. The adoption created the foundation from which she could build her life.One of the biggest changes was stability. A child needs more than talent to reach a high level in any sport. They need adults who can provide encouragement, transportation, time, money, emotional support and a safe place to return to after a difficult day. Biles found that support with Ron and Nellie.Nellie, in particular, became deeply involved in Biles’ life and eventually became the mother figure she knew. Biles has spoken about how her parents supported her ambitions and made sure she had what she needed to compete.That support became especially important once gymnastics entered her life. Biles first encountered gymnastics during a daycare field trip when she was around six years old. She began copying the movements of older gymnasts, and coaches noticed that she had unusual natural ability. Her family then supported her as she started taking gymnastics more seriously.It is easy to look at Biles today and see the medals, records and extraordinary routines. Her quote asks people to look much further back. Before any of those achievements, there was a child who needed a safe place to grow. Her grandparents helped provide that place.How did Ron and Nellie Biles help Simone build her future?Ron and Nellie did more than give Simone and Adria a home. They became active parts of the girls’ lives and supported their interests as they grew up.As Simone’s gymnastics career developed, the family continued to stand behind her. Nellie has spoken about creating a strong support system around Simone, including family traditions such as weekly dinners and attending church together. The family also traveled to support Biles during major competitions, showing that her achievements were never treated as something she had to experience alone.Ron also played an important role in Biles’ gymnastics journey. He and Nellie later opened the World Champions Centre in Spring, Texas, where Biles trained. The facility became another part of the environment that supported her development as an elite gymnast.But their influence was not only about gymnastics. The most important thing they gave Biles was the feeling that she belonged.That can be seen in a story from the time of the adoption. After the adoption papers were signed, Biles asked Nellie if she could call her “Mom.” For a young child, that simple question carried enormous meaning. It showed that Biles was beginning to see Nellie not simply as her grandmother’s wife, but as the person who would fill the role of her mother.Nellie has also described the emotional process of becoming a mother to children who were previously her grandchildren. She said there was a point when she realized she would do anything for them, and that was when she knew she was truly their mother.That bond helped shape the person Biles became. Her career required an extraordinary amount of discipline, but having people who believed in her gave her somewhere to find strength when things became difficult.What does Simone Biles’ quote teach us about success and the people behind it?The most powerful part of Biles’ quote is that she does not describe success as something she achieved completely by herself. Instead, she connects her journey to a decision made by other people when she was still a child.That is important because Biles’ career is often described through her individual achievements. She became a multiple Olympic gold medalist, a world champion and one of the most decorated gymnasts in history. At the Paris 2024 Olympics, she added more medals to a career that had already made her one of the biggest names in gymnastics.Yet behind every routine was a larger story.There was the child who experienced foster care. There was the grandfather who wanted to make sure she and Adria were cared for. There was Nellie, who became her mother and helped create a loving home. There was a family that supported her when gymnastics changed from something she enjoyed into a demanding career.Biles’ story also shows why success should not always be measured from the moment someone wins something. Sometimes the most important victory happens years before anyone is watching.For Biles, that turning point came when Ron and Nellie gave her a permanent home. It gave her the opportunity to grow, find gymnastics, develop her talent and eventually become the athlete the world knows today.Her words also carry a message for children who may be going through difficult situations. A difficult beginning does not necessarily decide how the rest of a person’s life will look. The right people, the right support and the right opportunities can change the direction of a life.That is what makes Biles’ quote so meaningful. She is not saying that adoption alone made her successful. She is recognizing what that moment gave her: stability, love, encouragement and the chance to discover her own potential.And perhaps that is the heart of her story. articles.body:
Hurricane Isaias is forecast to hammer the Pensacola area this weekend, forcing schools in north Florida (and Alabama and Mississippi) to scramble football schedules this week.

The hurricane is projected to make landfall in the Alabama or northwest Florida coast late Friday or in the wee hours of Saturday. But so far, only five changes have been made for original Week 8 games in the Orlando area — despite heavy rain that has drenched fields.

We'll be posting live updates from games right here. Check back often once games kick off.

Long before Isaias hovered over the game plans, state-ranked Orlando rivals Edgewater and Jones had to revamp their schedules to make room for their non-district downtown Orlando showdown. That game, originally scheduled for Sept. 18, was postponed due to stormy weather and is now set for Monday at Jones, starting at 6 p.m.

Jones (4-1, 1-0), ranked No. 3 in the Sentinel Super 16 Coaches Poll, shifted its crucial Class 4A District 6 home game against Lake Wales (5-1, 2-0) from Friday to Thursday to give the Tigers three days before facing Edgewater, No. 6 in the Super 16.

The Eagles (4-2, 2-0) moved their Class 6A District 6 home game against Olympia (3-5, 0-2) to Wednesday night and won 34-0 in what Edgewater head coach Patrick Browning said "was a monsoon all game."

Foundation Academy's road game against Providence School of Jacksonville was shifted from Friday to tonight for fear of heavy rains and winds. A number of Jacksonville area games were moved up.
