articles.title: Vikings suggested to call Dolphins and Chargers about making quarterback trade, but price is high
articles.summary: Should Minnesota consider it?
articles.body:
When teams are in strange quarterback positions, it typically gets viewed in a completely different light than anything else. Even for the Minnesota Vikings , who sit at 4-0, to say the quarterback play has been ideal this season would be unfair. As time goes on, it's clear the Vikings made the wrong decision by moving on from Sam Darnold.

It is what it is at this point, and the Vikings can't change it, but it is something to consider over the next couple of weeks, as others have suggested a quarterback trade could be possible.

Searching for options, one insider recently mentioned a couple of players who could be available. One was Malik Willis, the Miami Dolphins quarterback. Justin Herbert was also mentioned.

"I just don't think you have many options," Middlekauff said in an Oct. 6 video from "3 & OUT with John Middlekauff" about whether he sees the Vikings making a midseason trade for a QB, per Heavy .

"Who are you trading for? Would the Dolphins trade Malik Willis for a second-round pick? Could you offer three first-rounders for Herbert? If the team is just imploding and maybe they go winless and draft a quarterback, you would do that if you were Minnesota. I just don't really see your options."

Adding Herbert would definitely be the most intriguing option, though it remains uncertain whether the Los Angeles Chargers would even entertain it, even with decent draft capital involved.

The Chargers have been one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL to start this season, but that doesn't mean they want to move on from their starting quarterback.

articles.title: So, where do the Atlanta Braves go from here following another Postseason exit?
articles.summary: Well, at least it’s clear as to what needs to be improved. ‘How’ is the big question, though.
articles.body:
It's The Day After and now that we've all had some time to really take things into perspective, the obvious thing to do in times like this is to look forward. The good news is that following their exit in the NLDS at the hands of the Los Angeles Dodgers, it's pretty clear where the Atlanta Braves need to focus their improvement efforts on. The main question, however, is how are they going to do that in a way that tangibly changes things going forward?

For the most part, the Braves are going to be running it back. In order of compensation, Chris Sale, Austin Riley, Matt Olson, Spencer Strider, Ronald Acuña Jr. (team option), Robert Suarez, Sean Murphy, Jurickson Profar (Yep), Mike Yastrzemski, Michael Harris II, Reynaldo López and Ozzie Albies are all under contract for next season. Dylan Lee, James Karinchak, Joey Wentz, Michael Grove, Luke Williams and Bryce Elder are all eligible for arbitration. Spencer Schwellenbach, Grant Holmes, Drake Baldwin, Ray Kerr, Didier Fuentes, Dylan Dodd and Victor Mederos are still in pre-arbitration so they're under team control.

Now, it's tough to imagine what moves can be made considering that there's a pretty decent chance that the financial landscape of baseball is going to change significantly once the impending CBA negotiations and potentially-looming lockout is said and done with but no matter what, I'd imagine that the 2027 Braves are going to look similar to the 2026 Braves. Atlanta is locked in at catcher, first base, (very likely) second base, third base, center field and (very likely) right field, they'll have enough starting pitching to fill out a rotation from the names I listed above and their bullpen is likely going to have its key players returning as well.

There's an opportunity to run it back for the Braves and I'd imagine that Alex Anthopoulos would do so. Again, this is a team that won 94 games and the NL East Division and has made the Postseason in every season but one since winning the World Series in 2021 — and even in 2025, you could argue that the injury bug was the main culprit for how disastrous that season ended up being. This is still a solid core with players who have the potential to break out at any given moment, so there's no reason to even consider blowing it up. It's also clear that both Anthopoulos and Walt Weiss value clubhouse chemistry a ton and this clubhouse's chemistry is arguably as good as it gets around baseball, so that's another reason to not just cause an earthquake with the ballclub.

With that being said, it can't be denied that the offense has taken a precipitous drop since their historically-successful 2023 regular season — and it's not like there have been many changes with this squad since then. The Braves have gone from a MLB-leading 126 team wRC+ in 2023 to a 101 wRC+ in 2024, then 101 wRC+ again in 2025 before sliding down to a below-average 97 wRC+ in 2026. Acuña, Olson, Murphy, Riley, Albies, and Harris were all here in 2023 and the fact that the lineup has declined as much as it has is actually a bit strange considering that there are only two players in that group who are over 30: Murphy and Olson, and it's not like they're ancient, themselves.

I hate to do coaching speculation since 1) we're not privy to their contract situations and 2) we haven't heard anything suggesting that anybody's jobs could be in danger but it would also make sense if Tim Hyers' position as hitting coach could come into question considering the performance. Dodgers pitching staff or not, a Postseason performance like what we saw at the plate from the Braves is going to put the magnifying glass on what exactly is going on with the offense and when it comes to that, Hyers is the one who could end up taking the blame in a big way if the Braves do decide to make a change. That's purely speculation on my part but also I'm not the only one!

It's also difficult to envision any trades being made — again, they're locked in at a lot of positions for a lot of dollars and any trades would have to be of either the blockbuster variety or something at the very fringes. So with that in mind, the way that the Braves could address the situation is the ol' fashioned way: From within.

As it turns out, the Braves currently have two position player prospects on the farm who just so happen to play the positions that could fill the pressing positional needs for the Braves for the forseeable future. Eric Hartman really made a name for himself during this past minor league season and while the Braves did have him playing center field for the most part, he also spent time manning left field as well. Tate Southisene is another consensus Top 100 prospect who has done a solid job of improving on the farm system this season and sure enough, he's capable of playing shortstop as well.

Will they be ready in time for the 2027 season? That's a bit doubtful, considering that both prospects are estimated for a 2028 arrival according to MLB Pipeline. It's more of a long-term option but those two are coming and they could finally address two inconsistent spots on the roster that have dogged the Braves for a few years now.

The bridge options are appealing, though. I'd imagine that the Braves are going to try hard to bring back Mauricio Dubón for another season considering how valuable he was for them with both his versatility and being able to man the shortstop spot when needed. Left Field may be a trickier proposition — remember, Jurickson Profar was slated to be a full-time DH before he got caught enjoying too much of a balanced and nutritious breakfast everyday for the second season in a row and had to take an unpaid suspension for the entirety of the 2026 season. Yaz is still going to be around but again, he's certainly a platoon option rather than an everyday option. I'd imagine that they'll try to acquire another outfielder to form a platoon.

The main reason why I haven't mentioned trading as much so far is because of the contract status of a lot of the core players and also because again, there's a lot to consider when it comes to what baseball looks like after the labor war ends. There's not a lot to speculate on until that's figured out but again, I can't see other teams really having the appetite to attempt to "fix" Austin Riley with the contract that he's on and it's a safe assumption that the Braves are simply going to try to figure this out internally when it comes to improving the offense as a whole.

It's a tricky situation to be in if you're Alex Anthopoulos and anybody in this front office! The team on paper is fine but if they're going to take the next step and potentially pick up another World Series title during this current window that they're in, it's clear that they're going to need to find a way to hit more consistently — especially in the Postseason. This routine of the bats failing to show up in October for the past few playoff appearances is starting to get honestly tiring and concerning. Even if the level of competition ratchets up during the Postseason, a near team-wide power outage that the Braves sustained shouldn't be happening as consistently as it does for this team in the playoffs. It also started to rear its ugly head during this regular season as well (remember June?) and it's become clear that improving the offense should be the main focus going into the offseason.

How will they do that? There's still a ton of questions to be answered and we're still a little too early to be getting into specifics. But it's clear what needs to be done and hopefully we'll see them make progress on addressing those issues once everybody gets a chance to actually figure it out in the offseason. We'll see what happens.

articles.title: Ric Flair built decades of wrestling wealth: How The Nature Boy turned his legendary career into a lasting financial legacy beyond the ring
articles.summary: Explore the financial journey of Ric Flair, from wrestling legend to brand icon, as he navigates the complexities of wealth, legal disputes, and brand commercialization.
articles.body: Ric Flair’s financial story is far more complicated than the image of luxury that defined his wrestling character. As “The Nature Boy”, Flair spent decades presenting himself as a jet-flying, limousine-riding superstar, while his actual career combined championship success, international fame and an ability to remain commercially relevant across generations. WWE recognises Flair as a 16-time world champion and a two-time WWE Hall of Fame inductee.According to Celebrity Net Worth, Ric Flair’s net worth is estimated at $1 million, with the figure updated in September 2026. That estimate reflects a career that generated substantial income but was also affected by tax problems, medical expenses, divorces, business disputes and extravagant spending. His modern financial story therefore centres less on preserved wrestling wealth and more on the continuing commercial power of the Ric Flair name.Ric Flair built a lasting brand beyond WWE wrestling eraRic Flair’s greatest financial asset has arguably been the character he created around himself. The Nature Boy was not simply a ring name; it became a complete entertainment identity built around flamboyant robes, designer suits, luxury imagery, the famous “Woooo!” catchphrase and an exaggerated personality that remained recognisable far beyond professional wrestling.That identity developed alongside Flair’s rise through the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE. His championships and rivalries established sporting credibility, while his interviews and distinctive presentation gave promoters another reason to build major events around him. WWE’s official profile highlights his NWA and WCW championships, WWE Championship reigns and two WWE Hall of Fame inductions.The commercial value of that persona has endured because Flair became bigger than any single wrestling promotion. His name has appeared across merchandise, entertainment, appearances, licensing opportunities and popular culture. His influence even reached music, with the “Ric Flair Drip” phrase becoming a major hip-hop reference and introducing his identity to audiences who may never have followed his wrestling career.According to Celebrity Net Worth, however, the fortune generated by that fame did not remain intact. The publication cites tax liens, medical costs, divorces and extravagant spending as major factors behind the gap between Flair’s enormous career profile and his current estimated net worth.Ric Flair turned WWE fame into businessFlair eventually moved beyond relying solely on wrestling appearances. His modern strategy has centred on commercialising the elements that made The Nature Boy recognisable in the first place. That approach allowed his name to remain useful to brands even after his full-time wrestling career had ended.One of the clearest examples is WOOOOO! Energy. Energy to 54 On the Run locations across Missouri, while also outlining plans for additional flavours. The wrestling connection also became part of the business strategy. In 2023, All Elite Wrestling announced a multi-year deal involving Flair, while WOOOOO! Energy became AEW’s exclusive energy drink. The product was promoted through AEW venues and appeared around broadcasts, giving the brand direct access to wrestling fans.Flair also entered the cannabis business through Ric Flair Drip, a brand connected with Mike Tyson’s cannabis venture. Forbes noted Flair’s partnership with Tyson in the cannabis space while highlighting his wider effort to develop a second act around branding and storytelling.Ric Flair expanded earnings through brand venturesFlair’s modern income model demonstrates how retired entertainers can continue earning from recognition built during their active careers. Wrestling appearances, autograph sessions, merchandise, licensing and commercial partnerships allow the Nature Boy identity to remain monetisable without requiring a conventional full-time wrestling schedule.The difference between Flair’s peak wrestling years and his current business approach is particularly important. During his active career, his income was tied heavily to wrestling contracts, championship prominence, event appearances and the demanding touring schedule associated with major promotions. His modern model instead depends more heavily on the value of his name, image, catchphrase and cultural recognition.His ability to maintain relevance across different industries has also helped protect the Nature Boy character from becoming a nostalgia act solely. The WOOOOO! Energy expansion, for example, shows how a decades-old wrestling catchphrase can be repositioned as a consumer brand.At the same time, Flair’s business history illustrates the risks associated with commercialising a personal identity. Recent legal disputes have focused directly on control of his name, image, likeness and social media presence, making ownership of his personal brand a central financial issue.Ric Flair turned his persona into a WWE legacyThe latest chapter of Flair’s financial story has focused heavily on protecting and monetising the identity that took decades to build. In September 2026, Flair filed a lawsuit against talent agency FAM Networks seeking at least $10 million, alleging that he was misled into signing an agreement that gave the company extensive rights connected with his name, image, likeness and digital identity.According to the lawsuit, Flair was given only 14 minutes to review the agreement before signing it and alleges that promised commercial opportunities did not materialise as expected. He claims the arrangement resulted in significant lost revenue and disputes the extent of the rights he granted. The allegations remain claims in ongoing litigation and have not been established as facts in court.That dispute underlines the unusual financial position Flair occupies today. His wrestling career may be largely finished, but the character created during those decades remains a valuable commercial property. The same robes, catchphrase, personality and reputation that helped make him one of wrestling’s biggest stars can still be attached to products, appearances, media projects and licensing agreements.According to Celebrity Net Worth, Flair’s current estimated net worth is $1 million, a figure that illustrates the difference between lifetime earning power and retained wealth. His financial legacy is therefore not simply measured by how much money was earned during his wrestling peak, but by how effectively the Nature Boy identity can continue generating value.Flair’s story ultimately demonstrates that professional wrestling can create a form of intellectual property that survives long after championship reigns end. His career produced an instantly recognisable persona, and his post-wrestling ventures have repeatedly attempted to convert that recognition into commercial opportunities. articles.title: Chargers’ Justin Herbert suddenly named trade candidate for three first round picks
articles.summary: Should the Chargers consider it?
articles.body:
While the Los Angeles Chargers have arguably been the most disappointing team in the NFL this season at 0-4, it still feels like some crazy takes are flying around.

The 0-4 Chargers definitely haven't played the kind of football they hoped for entering this season, but saying they should move on from their franchise quarterback, Justin Herbert, still might not be the right idea.

While Herbert hasn't played well himself, a lot of that doesn't really fall on him. Some of it does, and Herbert has to be blamed for some of the problems we've seen over the past couple of years, though it's not crazy to say that if he were in a better system, he'd be a much better player.

As crazy as it might sound, he might be the perfect change-of-scenery candidate, with one insider recently suggesting that the Minnesota Vikings should be interested in him and the Chargers could get three first-round picks in return.

"I just don't think you have many options," Middlekauff said in an Oct. 6 video from "3 & OUT with John Middlekauff" about whether he sees the Vikings making a midseason trade for a QB, per Heavy .

"Who are you trading for? Would the Dolphins trade Malik Willis for a second-round pick? Could you offer three first-rounders for Herbert? If the team is just imploding and maybe they go winless and draft a quarterback, you would do that if you were Minnesota. I just don't really see your options."

If the Chargers were offered three first-round picks, as crazy as it might sound, it's definitely not a given that he'd be moved. Los Angeles would probably have to consider it, but it also has to feel like it has a franchise quarterback, and that might be worth more than three first-round picks.

Four-star safety and wide receiver recruit Nick Carroll has committed to the Georgia Bulldogs . Carroll, a member of the class of 2028, is Georgia 's third commitment in the junior class.

Carroll joins four-star tight end Asa Wall and the nation's top quarterback, Jayden Wade , in Georgia's class of 2028. The four-star is a great addition for coach Kirby Smart and company, who have the nation's No. 6 recruiting class in the 2028 cycle.

Carroll is a Peach State product. The 5-foot-10, 170-pound athlete is ranked as the No. 48 recruit in the nation. Carroll plays high school football for Toombs County in Lyons, Georgia. Carroll is ranked as the fourth-best safety in the class of 2028 and the fifth-best recruit in Georgia.

Georgia is not done recruiting in the class of 2028. The Dawgs are also predicted to land a commitment from four-star offensive tackle recruit Koehn Dial.

Carroll committed to Georgia despite having scholarship offers from other college football powers like Tennessee, Penn State and Indiana. The four-star posted an elite sophomore season where he scored 11 touchdowns, had seven interceptions and posted over 700 receiving yards. The Toombs County star is versatile and can return kicks in addition to playing offense and defense.

articles.title: What Will Be The Keys To The Brewers Taking Down The Dodgers In 2026 NLCS?
articles.summary: FOX Sports' Eric Karros has the blueprint for how the Milwaukee Brewers can finally beat the Los Angeles Dodgers in the playoffs.
articles.body: "So, we meet again, Buzz Lightyear … for the last time!" For the fourth time in nine seasons, the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers will square off in the National League playoffs, as the top-seeded Brewers (103-59) defeated the San Diego Padres in the NL Division Series and the second-seeded Dodgers (100-62) beat the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS. But the Dodgers have come out on top in each of these two teams' playoff meetings (2018 NLCS, 2020 wild-card round and 2025 NLCS), including a four-game sweep of the Brewers in last year's NLCS. How do the Brewers flip the script? FOX Sports MLB Analyst Eric Karros has the answers. "They come to play every single day. They grind; they don't give away anything. Offensively, I don't know if it's necessarily the hitting part as much as it's controlling the strike zone, and that means don't expand, don't chase pitches out of the zone, take your walks, be patient and just kind of wear down this Dodgers' pitching staff," Karros said about the Brewers' offense in an appearance on Thursday's edition of "The Herd. "That's really the MO that they're going to have to create offensively." While they ultimately advanced to the NLCS on Wednesday night, the Brewers only scored 13 runs across their four games against the Padres in the NLDS. Last year, the Brewers scored just four runs against the Dodgers in the 2025 NLCS en route to being swept despite being third in MLB in both runs and hits in the regular season. In the 2026 regular season, Milwaukee was first in the sport in hits (1,422) and on-base percentage (.341), tied for first in batting average (.258), second outright in runs (832) and tied for 10th in slugging percentage (.403). Remarkably, though, the Brewers were tied for 28th in home runs (154). Second baseman Brice Turang has been the star of the show for Milwaukee this season, posting 23 defensive runs saved at the middle infield position, driving in a team-high 100 runs and posting 7.3 wins above replacement, which was third among MLB position players. Elsewhere, primary first baseman Jake Bauers hit a team-high 26 home runs, while driving in 86 runs and posting a .484 slugging percentage; left fielder Jackson Chourio totaled 25 home runs, 75 RBIs, 23 stolen bases and 4.9 wins above replacement over 127 games, while posting a .291/.351/.487 slash line; Chourio hit a walk-off, two-run single in a 2-2 count with two outs in Game 2 of the NLDS; William Contreras drove in 94 runs in the regular season, which led MLB catchers, and hit two home runs in the NLDS. All that said, as productive as Milwaukee's bats have been, pitching remains the backbone of its operation. The Brewers' starting rotation was second in MLB in opponent batting average (.220), third outright in strikeouts (907), tied for third in WHIP (1.14) and fifth outright in ERA (3.61). Ace Jacob Misiorowski posted a 1.80 ERA, an 0.80 WHIP, a 232 ERA+ and 252 strikeouts, which were all NL-bests, over 30 starts; fellow right-hander Logan Henderson recorded a 2.47 ERA, an 0.84 WHIP and 110 strikeouts over 18 starts. Meanwhile, Milwaukee's bullpen was third in ERA (3.40) and opponent batting average (.223) and tied for fifth in WHIP (1.23). Of course, the Brewers are facing a potent Dodgers team that's among the upper echelon of teams, if not at the top of the mountain in terms of depth. With the bats, Los Angeles, which features the likes of Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker, among many others, was second in the regular season in slugging percentage (.424), third in batting average (.257) and on-base percentage (.338), fourth in runs (801) and tied for fourth in hits (1,399). The Dodgers also had the fourth-fewest strikeouts in the sport (1,267). On the starting pitching front, the Dodgers were second in ERA (3.43) and opponent batting average (.220), tied for third in WHIP (1.14) and fourth outright in strikeouts (904). Los Angeles, which already featured 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell and right-hander Tyler Glasnow, acquired back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers at the MLB trade deadline. Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3 due to knee inflammation, but he has remained the Dodgers' primary designated hitter. "From a pitching standpoint, they've got Misiorowski, who's as good as anybody and actually dominates left-handers. He's much better against left-handed hitting [.114 opponent batting average] than he is against right-handers [.209 opponent batting average]. The Dodgers are top-heavy on the left side. That could help Milwaukee," Karros said about the Brewers' pitching staff. "They also have Logan Henderson. At the end of the day, this series is going to come down to the Brewers' bullpen and matchup against the Dodgers' depth position player-wise and what [Dodgers manager] Dave Roberts creates." Milwaukee went 4-3 against Los Angeles in the regular season, with both teams winning a series in the opponent's home ballpark. Game 1 of the 2026 NLCS is on Sunday night, with the entire series airing on FOX networks. "I'm looking forward to the series as a fan. I think it's going to be a great series," Karros said.

articles.title: What Man City charges anger Liverpool before Premier League game?
articles.summary: Clubs reportedly want reimbursements after Man City charges – one of those, Liverpool, are first opponent in fallout.
articles.body:
Manchester City are preparing for their first football match since receiving a guilty verdict for multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules and – of course – their opponent on Sunday is one of the clubs that hold grievances over their losses during the seasons in question.

Liverpool’s Anfield crowd is expected to deliver an angry reception for the Premier League clash, and City manager Enzo Maresca and his players must prepare for the backlash to continue throughout the game itself.

City have protested their innocence and have appealed the verdict that went against them on more than 100 charges of financial wrongdoing.

Still, the scandal remains the biggest in the history of club football’s richest, most competitive and most popular league, and the backlash from the stands is likely to linger long after any appeal outcome or potential punishments are finalised.

The current crop of players and staff are quite simply going to have to face the music for charges that stretch from 2009 to 2018.

The fact that their opening match after the international window, when the guilty verdict was delivered, is at Anfield is something that a scriptwriter may even pause to think is outlandish.

“If they want an understanding of how angry the game ⁠is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe,” former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville declared recently on The Overlap podcast.

“I suspect there may be banners, there will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield… it will be a brutal day.”

Why are Liverpool set to give Man City an angry reception?

Of all the clubs that finished second best to City since the Abu Dhabi buyout, Liverpool will argue that they have been among the hardest hit.

There is a growing feeling that any titles that City are stripped of should be awarded to their nearest rivals, or defeated finalists, during the period investigated.

For Liverpool, however, their two closest calls with City came after 2018.

Under former coach Jurgen Klopp, Liverpool won the Premier League in 2020, but the team also finished second to Pep Guardiola’s City by one point in the 2018-19 and 2021-22 seasons.

Both were memorable title races that raised the bar in terms of points earned and the standard of football played.

Neither will see Liverpool retrospectively awarded the title if the Premier League does indeed choose to go down that path regarding honours won in the seasons that were under investigation.

Liverpool’s fans will assert, and most likely vociferously argue on Sunday, that what helped City reach that level was nearly a decade of rule-breaking, as the independent panel has found.

Liverpool do, however, have a claim to at least one title in the period in question.

The Reds, under Brendan Rodgers, finished runners-up by two points to City in 2013-2014 – Steven Gerrard’s infamous slip in a match against Chelsea the moment etched on everyone’s memory from that campaign.

It left the Anfield faithful continuing their wait for a first top-flight title since 1990.

Only weeks earlier, Gerrard was the star of the show as Liverpool beat City 3-2 to seemingly put one hand on the elusive title.

Any retrospective award of titles could see club legend Gerrard finally hold a Premier League winner’s medal.

Do any of Man City’s current setup remain from the period of the charges?

Aside from Phil Foden, who is suspended for the match, no current member of City’s squad even played for the club from 2009-2018.

Enzo Maresca, who was a youth-team coach for City in 2020-21 and was assistant to Guardiola in 2022-2023, took over as City’s first-team manager only in June.

Still, they will be the ones bearing the brunt of the widespread discontent from fan bases up and down the country in the coming months.

What will be intriguing is who from City’s ownership or board attends the Liverpool game.

How much will the matter weigh on the players under the most intense pressure? And what will be the reaction of City’s match-going supporters, with the future of their club so uncertain – the potential sanctions include a huge points deduction, even expulsion from the Premier League – and the violations of its ownership clear for all to see in the commission’s verdict?

City lead the league with five wins from five games – all of which were played when the club was being accused of those financial breaches.

Now the guilty verdict has arrived, it’s time to see the impact on the team – and the reaction of its rivals.

articles.title: French giants Bordeaux relegated to sixth tier for financial irregularities
articles.summary: Six-time French champions Bordeaux, the club where Zinedine Zidane made his name, to play in sixth tier after sanctions.
articles.body:
Six-time French champions Bordeaux, sanctioned in the summer for financial irregularities, will play in the sixth tier of French football this season, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league confirmed on Thursday.

Bordeaux were sanctioned for failing to provide the roughly 10 million euros ($11.6m) needed for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 financial years and to meet debt payments.

Once one of France’s leading football clubs and the team where the country’s new head coach, Zinedine Zidane, made his name, Bordeaux was sold last month for a symbolic one euro to US-based investment group Park Bench, which agreed to take on the remaining debt.

Two days after appearing before the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league oversight commission, which approved its recovery budget and issued “a positive opinion on their possible participation in Regional 1”, the club was unanimously approved to play in the top regional tier.

“Rebuilding can now begin,” said Dominique Delport, the new president chosen by Park Bench, speaking to the AFP news agency.

The new owners are due in commercial court on October 20 to ratify the new continuation plan, which now runs over 12 years, with the debt halved from 26 million to 13 million euros.

The team is largely amateur, though the club can field five players on professional contracts, one of whom will be former Ligue 1 striker Baptiste Guillaume.

The club has produced many big names of French football, including academy products Bixente Lizarazu and Christophe Dugarry, who both played alongside Zidane in the 1998 World Cup-winning team.

More than a decade earlier, Alain Giresse and Jean Tigana were part of a celebrated France midfield that won the 1984 European Championship.

However, they were relegated to Ligue 2 in 2022 and then placed under judicial restructuring in 2024, which caused them to relinquish their professional status and their highly rated academy.

articles.title: Jeff Cannonball cause of death: What happened to the wrestler who died at 39?
articles.summary: Independent wrestling star Jeff Cannonball, whose real name was Jeff Guerriero, has died at 39 after battling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
articles.body: Independent wrestling star Jeff Cannonball, whose real name was Jeff Guerriero, has died at 39 after battling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). His wife, fellow professional wrestler Terra Calaway, confirmed his death in a social media tribute on Thursday, October 8, 2026. She revealed that he died at around 2 a.m., less than an hour after they watched his favourite comedy, Dirty Work. Cannonball announced his ALS diagnosis in May 2025. Known for his hardcore wrestling career, he competed for several independent promotions, including Hardcore Hustle Organization (H2O), Game Changer Wrestling (GCW) and Major League Wrestling (MLW).Terra Calaway Remembers Jeff Guerriero in Emotional TributeIn her tribute, Calaway recalled watching Dirty Work, the 1998 comedy starring Norm Macdonald and Artie Lange, with her husband during his final hours. The film helped lighten the mood after a difficult day.“Wednesday night into Thursday morning, I put on Dirty Work on the tv to help lighten the mood of a rough day. Norm Macdonald and Artie Lange in a Bob Saget directed comedy movie. Jeff’s favorite movie with two of the three comedians he thought were the funniest men on the planet- Norm and Don Rickles. All it was missing was Tom Green.”Calaway also remembered what Cannonball said after Macdonald died in 2021, sharing a line that now carries a painful meaning for the family.“When Norm passed away in 2021, Jeff said that the funniest man on the planet was gone. He was wrong.”She then shared the time of her husband’s death, explaining that he passed away shortly after the movie ended.“Less than an hour after the end of the movie on Thursday, October 8th, 2026 at 2am is the day the funniest man on the planet has gone.”Calaway spoke about the life they shared over 10 years of marriage and their son, Milo. She described her husband as someone whose humour and personality left a lasting mark on the people around him.“Jeff Guerriero, the funniest, wittiest, most charismatic man I have ever had the privilege of knowing let alone get to marry, spend 10 years with, and create a little clone of in our son Milo, has passed away after his battle with ALS. His impact on his friends, his community, and the world is endless. Jeff Guerriero and Jeff Cannonball will live forever.”She also wrote about the pain of losing him and her promise to keep his memory alive while raising their son.“I will mourn him for every single day of my life while honoring him by raising a son he would be so incredibly proud of. My soul and heart are broken beyond repair.”Calaway ended her message with a personal expression of love and gratitude for their time together.“I love you Jeff. 10 years was not enough, but they are years I will cherish forever. In every timeline, in every universe, in every life, I would do all of this over again as long as it meant I got that time with you.”Jeff Cannonball’s Wrestling Career and LegacyCannonball began wrestling professionally in 2010 and became known for his work in hardcore wrestling. He was a two-time H2O Danny Havoc Hardcore Champion and also competed for GCW and MLW.His death has brought sadness to the independent wrestling community, where he built a name through his performances and connections with fellow wrestlers. articles.body: Corey Pavin reveals wife Lisa’s cancer ‘never went away completely’ months after her final chemotherapy sessionFormer US Open champion Corey Pavin has revealed that his wife, Lisa Pavin, is receiving further cancer treatment after doctors found that her cancer had not completely gone away. Lisa, 52, began CAR-T cell therapy on Tuesday, October 6, following several visits to the Mayo Clinic over the past two months. Pavin, 66, shared the update on Instagram, saying he and his family were “hoping and praying” that the treatment would work. He has not revealed the type of cancer Lisa is battling.Corey Pavin shares Lisa Pavin’s cancer update and CAR-T treatment detailsPavin had shared encouraging news about Lisa’s treatment earlier this year. In February, he announced that she had completed her final round of chemotherapy, giving their family a reason to hope for better days ahead. However, the latest update shows that her fight against cancer is continuing.On Tuesday, Pavin explained that the cancer had not completely gone away, despite the earlier treatment. He also shared that Lisa had started CAR-T therapy after spending the past two months visiting the Mayo Clinic for medical care.“Seven plus months ago, I posted that @lisap0810 had her last chemotherapy,” Pavin wrote on Instagram. “We found out a couple months ago that her cancer never went away completely.“Over the last two months and after multiple visits to the Mayo Clinic, Lisa is getting her CAR-T infusion today. We are hoping and praying that this will kick her cancer’s a**!“The emotional and physical toll fighting cancer is immense, and I’m so proud of Lisa’s courage, attitude and perseverance! And much gratitude to all of Lisa’s friends who have reached out to her for your prayers and support which has helped more than you will ever know!”CAR-T therapy, short for chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, is a form of immunotherapy. It uses a patient’s T cells, which are part of the immune system, to recognise and attack cancer cells. The treatment is used for certain types of cancer, although Pavin has not shared which type Lisa has.Along with his message, the former golfer posted several pictures of Lisa smiling in her hospital bed. Another image showed the couple embracing aboard a private jet. The photos accompanied his update on her treatment and his appreciation for the people who have supported their family.Corey Pavin and Lisa Pavin’s family life amid her cancer battleCorey and Lisa married in 2003 and have an 18-year-old daughter, Alexis. Despite the difficult period at home, the family recently marked an important moment as Alexis began college in California.In September, Pavin shared a picture of himself and Lisa dropping their daughter off ahead of her first day at college. His message showed how proud they were of her as she started this new chapter.“@alexispavin, tomorrow is your first day of college!! We are so proud of you and the young woman you have become!“We are sure you are going to thrive out in Cali. We will miss your love, wit, “charm”, and your unique (and wonderful) personality! And most of all, we will miss you. We love you more than you will ever know!”Pavin has also continued to compete in golf while Lisa undergoes treatment. Last month, he played in the Sanford International at Minnehaha Country Club in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. articles.title: 2 Jacksonville schools face playoff ban following football fight
articles.summary: The Florida High School Athletic Association placed two Duval County public schools on restrictive probation, excluding them from football playoffs.
articles.body:
The Florida High School Athletic Association placed both Baldwin and Parker on restrictive probation in football for a fight late in the teams' game on Oct. 2, a punishment that would render both teams ineligible for the regional playoffs beginning in November.

The FHSAA confirmed to the USA TODAY Network on Oct. 8 that it had issued restrictive probation against both schools. Any additional penalties, such as fines or player suspensions, were not yet specified.

It is not yet clear whether either school intends to appeal. E-mail messages sent Oct. 8 to both athletic departments were not returned as of late Thursday afternoon.

Under FHSAA Operational Bylaw 10.1.2 (d) (2), restrictive probation carries "the same penalties as administrative probation [including reprimand, fine and warning], with the additional consequence of restriction from participation in championship competition in one or more sports, or other restrictions deemed appropriate by the Executive Director, for one or more calendar years."

The Times-Union is awaiting the receipt of additional documentation connected with the case.

What happened in Parker vs. Baldwin football?

The incident occurred near the end of the teams' Week 7 game, which ended in a 27-12 victory for Baldwin . A short video clip recorded from the opposite side of the stadium and posted to YouTube showed jawing and some shoving that involved numerous players, escalating to several players fighting on the ground.

Parker (0-7) stood 15th of 16 teams in Region 1-3A, with playoff qualification unlikely even before the penalties. However, Baldwin (2-4), although only third in District 3-2A behind Bolles and Jackson, occupied what would have been the eighth and final postseason berth in Region 1-2A.

If Baldwin is excluded from postseason, the door would open for a Panhandle school like Panama City Rutherford (2-4) or Freeport (3-4), both just behind Baldwin in the MaxPreps rating formula used to allocate at-large playoff selections.

The Baldwin-Parker altercation was among several fight-marred Week 7 games involving Florida high schools. Deltona and Matanzas played an Oct. 1 game that ended in a brawl during postgame handshakes, and Miami Carol City had 15 players suspended for their role in an Oct. 2 fight against Grayson of Georgia.

Carol City also received restrictive probation on Oct. 8, which would keep a state-ranked Chiefs team out of the FHSAA playoffs. The FHSAA assessed similar penalties against Deltona and Matanzas on Oct. 8, as reported by the Daytona Beach News-Journal.

articles.title: What Changes Should the Astros Make to Their Bullpen This Offseason
articles.summary: Houston's bullpen faced injuries and role changes in 2026. What needs to happen before 2027?
articles.body:
Image 1: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images, Image 2-4: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images

The Houston Astros dealt with their fair share of injuries and setbacks this past season. One of their biggest weaknesses was pitching. Many of the Astros' starters struggled, whether they couldn't settle into the starting role or just couldn't give the team the length they needed.

On top of the rotation's struggles, the Astros were also without their clutch closer, Josh Hader , who was sidelined with left biceps tendinitis. Bryan Abreu stepped into the closer role, but he struggled to deliver the same level of consistency that Hader brought to the mound.

As the Astros' starters returned to the rotation and Hader came back, the team looked like a different animal on the mound. Hader is the guy to close things out with a save.

Despite all these struggles, they held on by a thread. That kind of wear and tear is not sustainable. The bullpen wasn't always holding things together either. On more than one occasion, it turned into an unexpected bullpen game.

So the question is: What does the Astros' bullpen need for 2027? Better arms, more consistent arms, or simply less wear and tear on the bullpen and more length from their starters?

First, let's look at what went right. That would be Hader and his performance; he had 26 saves on the season.

Here is a look at his 2026 regular-season stats:

4–2 W–L, 1.01 ERA, 45 G, 26 SV, 44.2 IP, 55 SO, 0.76 WHIP.

Hader might be excellent, but he can't do it alone. They really need another clutch reliever like Hader. Abreu struggled when Hader was out, but once Hader returned, Abreu showed some improvement. Abreu had an up-and-down season; if he can develop consistency during the offseason, that could be a game-changer for the Astros bullpen.

Then they have AJ Blubaugh. Despite his brutal outing in the first game of the postseason, Blubaugh actually had a strong season. He pitched more innings than any other reliever in MLB. Unfortunately, some of his bad moments overshadowed his strong ones. His worst outing came as an opener in the Wild Card series, so keeping him as a reliever seems like the move.

Then, there is Steven Okert, who had the best season of his career. It was unfortunate that his season ended with injury, but he was throwing from the mound at the end of the regular season, so he should be back up and running for 2027.

Miguel Ullola made his major league debut this season, earlier than expected due to so many injuries. Still, it allowed him to prove he can hold his own on the major league mound. The young player, once one of the Astros' top prospects, is definitely an arm to watch.

As for the rest of the bullpen, they are either young or just had a rough season. They're worth evaluating and definitely have room for improvement, but they could make their mark or stage a comeback depending on the situation.

So what should Houston prioritize with the bullpen this offseason? Possibly adding a strong middle reliever and improving the talent they already have. A little consistency goes a long way and could completely change the Astros bullpen.

articles.title: Browns QB Dillon Gabriel Gets Blunt Response Amid Return
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have a decision to make with Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders. The post Browns QB Dillon Gabriel Gets Blunt Response Amid Return appea...
articles.body:
Dillon Gabriel is back on the practice field, but some have little interest in seeing him move up the Cleveland Browns' quarterback depth chart.

Gabriel's return from a back injury has renewed discussion about who should back up Deshaun Watson. With Cleveland riding a three-game winning streak, the question carries different stakes than it did when the Browns were trying to climb out of an ugly season-opening loss with low expectations.

During a discussion on ESPN Cleveland, Browns reporter Tony Grossi saw little reason to expect a change behind Watson.

"I think it will be Shedeur, as long as Watson is healthy," Grossi said. "Why wouldn't it be? He's been No. 2 since September."

Aaron Goldhammer agreed that Sanders would be his choice for an extended stretch. A brief appearance to keep the offense moving while Watson is sidelined, however, gave him more to consider.

"The dynamic of the room has changed because now the Browns are winning. If you had someone taking over for seven games, I want Shedeur," Goldhammer said. "If you need someone to jump in during the third quarter for a series while someone is in the medical tent, I wonder if it'd be Dillon Gabriel. If you're trying to win…"

"No. I've seen enough of Dillon Gabriel," Rizzo said.

Browns Have Time to Make Dillon Gabriel Decision

The Browns cleared Gabriel to return to practice Tuesday , opening a 21-day window to evaluate the second-year quarterback before deciding whether to activate him from injured reserve.

Gabriel missed Cleveland's first four games with a back injury . Returning to practice does not put him back on the 53-man roster, and the Browns do not have to activate him for Sunday's matchup with the New York Jets .

Head coach Todd Monken offered little indication that a decision was imminent. Asked Wednesday whether he felt any urgency to make Gabriel active, Monken answered, "Not really."

Monken said the Browns would evaluate Gabriel's back and get him work through individual drills and scout-team reps. When the discussion turned to potentially carrying four quarterbacks on the active roster, he again pointed to the time available.

"I don't have to feel anything at this point. We still have three weeks," Monken said .

That patience should not be confused with a lack of interest in Gabriel. Monken also praised his performance in the preseason finale and described him as "another coach on the field."

Browns Can Weigh QB Trade Without Forcing a Move

Trading Gabriel or Sanders would be one way to clear the QB room congestion . But Cleveland would need to weigh the return against the value of keeping another quarterback who already knows the offense.

There is also rookie Taylen Green to consider. Keeping Watson, Sanders, Gabriel and Green would require four spots on the active roster once Gabriel is activated, but it would allow the Browns to retain their depth and continue developing their young passers.

Carrying four quarterbacks remains uncommon, though Cleveland would have plenty of recent company. The Atlanta Falcons, Minnesota Vikings, Philadelphia Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers all kept four on their initial 53-man rosters this season.

There is a cost to using an extra roster spot at quarterback, particularly when injuries create needs elsewhere. But a crowded room alone does not make a trade worthwhile. A modest offer might be less valuable to Cleveland than keeping another option behind Watson.

articles.title: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Players Limited Ahead of Bills Matchup
articles.summary: Multiple key players on the Los Angeles Rams were limited ahead of the matchup with the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to face the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, and there are several players they may be without for the matchup.

During media availability on Thursday, Rams head coach Sean McVay offered updates via the injury report.

Per McVay, cornerback Jaylen Watson, defensive end Aaron Donald, and tight end Colby Parkinson were all limited to start the week.

Watson suffered a dislocated shoulder in Week 3 that led to his missing Week 4. Donald has a back issue that appeared ahead of Week 4, and he was made to rest instead of pushing through the injury.

Parkinson has been dealing with knee and shoulder injuries that also kept him out for Week 4, and he remains working through both ailments.

McVay also revealed that many other players did not practice on Thursday.

Linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), linebacker Josaiah Stewart (groin), safety Quentin Lake (hip), linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder), and wide receiver Davante Adams (veteran rest).

The Rams are still operating with a loss at the tight end position, as Terrance Ferguson was placed on IR due to a nagging ankle injury. Parkinson missed Week 4, and being limited does not mean he will miss Week 5, but still being injured is not great.

This leaves Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and rookie Max Klare as the healthy options.

Linebacker is also getting a bit thin with backup Stuart dealing with a hamstring, Stewart having a groin injury, and Landman also dealing with a shoulder.

All of their statuses right now do not mean they will not be upgraded by the final injury report on Saturday; it just means that they have currently missed practice.

One of the players that the Rams may need more than others is Donald . The pass rush did experience a big leap in Week 4 as linebacker Byron Young rifled off 2.5 sacks, and helped to seal with the win against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Bills may seek to stop Young, which would open more opportunities for Donald. This is assuming that he is healthy.

Donald is still working his way back to full action after a two-year layoff due to his retirement. Once he gets going fully, he could be a nightmare for offsenses.

That kind of pass rush is needed against a quarterback like Josh Allen, who can gun the ball downfield, but also rushes better than any other passer in the league.

This is just one of three injury reports, and the hope for the Rams is that many of those players are upgraded in the next two days.

articles.title: Michigan Basketball’s national title run ‘built’ Elliot Cadeau, Trey McKenney for bigger roles
articles.summary: Michigan Basketball’s national championship run last year “built” Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney for bigger roles.
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines took home the national championship last season behind the most dominant frontcourt in the country, but backcourt tandem Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney also played a pivotal part in cutting down the nets.

A year later, Cadeau and McKenney are set to step into bigger roles and become the leaders of the program this season. The confidence and experience that they gained from the national title run was invaluable and will lead to success this year.

"We definitely feel like there's more expectations on us and bigger roles for us," Cadeau said at Big Ten Media Day. "We're just really excited for it and very confident in ourselves for sure, and we're going to lead even more this season."

"Me and Elliot are definitely prepared for this year," McKenney told the media. "Last year, our team was so talented and we weren't asked to do as much as we could have done, but I think this season, we'll be able to show more of our game."

There wasn't a bigger boost in confidence across the country than what Cadeau experienced at Michigan last season. Cadeau went from a frustrating end to his time with North Carolina to being named the Final Four Most Outstanding Player.

"I feel like my whole life has built up to this year in a way," Cadeau explained. "In my first three years in college, I didn't really have the ball in my hands that much. I think this year, I'll have the ball more and I'm just very excited for it."

Cadeau was fourth in the Big Ten with 5.9 assists per game last year, while notching career-highs in points (10.5) and 3-point percentage (37.6). In the national title game, Cadeau dropped a game-high 19 points to lead Michigan to victory.

"We feel like when the team needs us at certain moments, we have the confidence to step up," Cadeau told the media. "Whether that's getting our other teammates involved or us scoring, we both feel like we can always make those plays."

Meanwhile, McKenney steadily improved throughout his freshman year and eventually emerged as a go-to player for the Wolverines in crunch time — culminating in him knocking down the game-sealing shot in the national championship game.

"He's always had a great maturity about his game and an understanding that you can only be as good as how hard you work for it," head coach Mike Boynton said when asked about McKenney. "Winning has always been the highest priority for him."

McKenney scored 9.9 points per game and shot a red-hot 39.1% mark from beyond the arc in his freshman campaign. In a lot of ways, McKenney was the x-factor for Michigan as the Wolverines went 26-0 when he scored in double figures.

Both players were named to the 2026 All-Big Ten Preseason Team so there's no doubt Cadeau and McKenney have high expectations this year. If the national title run was any indication, Cadeau and McKenney are ready to shine in bigger roles.

"Our experience is more in the backcourt this year with Elliot and Trey being the leaders of this group," Boynton said. "Both are among our hardest working guys. They set a great tone and we have great energy in our building because of that."

Now, Cadeau and McKenney hope to take the momentum that they finished last season with and carry it into this year. The Michigan backcourt has proven they have what it takes to excel in bigger roles, and lead the team on and off the court.

articles.title: How ‘conflict’ created by Giannis Antetokounmpo-Klay Thompson duo will boost Heat’s offense
articles.summary: MIAMI – With the fanbase anticipating the impact Giannis Antetokounmpo will have on the Miami Heat, the same can be said for Klay Thompson, as the two playe...
articles.body:
MIAMI – With the fanbase anticipating the impact Giannis Antetokounmpo will have on the Miami Heat, the same can be said for Klay Thompson , as the two players heading into the season are sure to play a huge role. As many expect the best versions of each player on the Heat , head coach Erik Spoelstra would give insight into how the two on the floor together fit so well.

In Miami's preseason debut in last Saturday's 129-105 win over the Toronto Raptors, both Antetokounmpo and Thompson started the game, though the stat sheet for the latter might be deceiving.

As Antetokounmpo impressed in the 14 minutes, recording nine points on three of three shooting from the field, three of four from the free-throw line, to go along with seven assists and four rebounds, Thompson didn't record any points in the outing.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Heat's Erik Spoelstra explains the positive "conflict" with the newcomers

However, it was clear to see that Toronto blanketed Thompson on defense, not allowing him to get an open shot, which gave more room for Antetokounmpo to operate. Spoelstra would say to ClutchPoints that "conflict" from defenses with the two newcomers will benefit the team.

"Well, the defense. You know, you're talking about a guy that was an elite defender over the course of his career," Spoelstra said before Thursday's home preseason opener against the New Orleans Pelicans. "So even at this age, he's smart. He's big. He knows where to be, and he takes the challenge. It's very important to him to depend on that side of the floor."

"And offensively, it's reputation versus reputation," Spoelstra continued. "That's the way we looked at it the other night. They both have great resumes. You know, Giannis has a reputation where you have to have multiple guys in front of them. Clay has a reputation where you don't ever take a body off him. So it's two conflicting things, and we want to try to maximize that the best that we can."

Heat's Klay Thompson, Giannis Antetokounmpo talk dynamic

There's no denying that Thompson's resume speaks for itself, as the four-time NBA champion with the Golden State Warriors is one of the most decorated three-point shooters of all time. Thompson would say after Monday's practice that the opposing defense is "respect."

"It means a lot to me," Thompson said. "You have to earn that. I've been on the defensive side of the ball where you do play a great scorer. And it's like your natural instinct to hug up on him. It's like you can't give this guy any space. He's too great of a player. And for me, I got to use that to my advantage, whether it's screening for my teammates or flying off screens or just spacing the floor. And I think that's why Spo [Spoelstra] and Mr. [Pat] Riley brought me here is for that point, just to be able to give guys operating room and make crucial shots when it matters most."

For Antetokounmpo, he's not used to not having the sole attention on defense, saying how he is used to "guys that build a wall," but Thompson adds another layer to the offense.

"It's just weird," Antetokounmpo said Monday. "Usually I always have guys on me, guys that build a wall. But there wasn't. With Klay, I think there was maybe one or two plays that he was wide open. One of them, I missed him, but he wasn't open. His guy was glued to him. "So if you know that you have a guy like that, who is one of probably, if not the best, second-greatest shooter of all time on the court with you, I think it makes the game a lot easier for you. When he's open, you've got to deliver the ball. When he's not open, you play four-against-four, more spacing, able to make plays for yourself, for your teammates."

At any rate, Antetokounmpo and Thompson will continue to get acclimated to Miami as the preseason rolls along ahead of the regular-season opener on Oct. 21 against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

• Out: Will not play, 0% chance to play.

• Doubtful: Unlikely to play, 25% chance to play.

• Questionable: Uncertain to play, 50% chance to play.

• Probable: Probable to play, 75% chance to play.

Per SEC policy, schools must accurately designate players' participation status. If the school has knowledge that a player may not be able to participate in the upcoming game for any reason (injury, illness, suspension, ineligibility or personal matter), it must report it.

Failure to do so will subject schools to potential penalties ranging from $25,000 for a first offense to $100,000 for a third and further offenses.

articles.title: Richard Sherman spreads wild Joey Porter Jr. illness theory on TNF
articles.summary: Former NFL star Richard Sherman questioned the reason Joey Porter Jr., who was ruled out with illness, would not play for the Cowboys.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys entered their Week 5 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night without newly acquired Joey Porter Jr. According to multiple reports, the fourth-year cornerback, who was shown on Prime Video's pre-game stream entering the AT&T Stadium locker room, was not available for the game due to sickness . NFL Network reported he had a virus and had been vomiting prior to kickoff.

Prime Video analyst Richard Sherman, formerly an All-Pro corner in the league himself, was far more skeptical regarding Porter's absence.

"I'm very interested in how this is gonna go," Sherman said on the pre-game set, dramatically eating popcorn for effect.

"The Dallas Cowboys are dealing with a little bit of what the Pittsburgh Steelers were dealing with. Hey, is he gonna play? Is he not? Is he sick? Is he not? Is his back hurt? Is it not? Negotiations, this is a business."

NFL Week 4 highlights, reactions and biggest moments around the league

Porter was acquired from the Steelers on Oct. 1 for a sixth-round pick in next year's draft and a Round 2 selection in 2028 after he was unable to reach a long-term extension in Pittsburgh, which historically does not negotiate with players once a season starts.

Porter did not play for the Steelers this season, citing a back injury, but debuted for the Cowboys in their Week 4 win against the Houston Texans.
